title: Formal phrases of means: a través de, por medio de, mediante

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *mediante* from B1 Unit 24: a formal phrase that says by what means something is done, and a noun follows it directly. *Por medio de* and *a través de* work in the same way. They are useful for trade, because goods travelled through ports and by means of fleets.

sections.title: By what means?
rows: *a través de* + noun: through a place or a channel

items.spanish: Los productos viajaban solo por medio del puerto de Sevilla.
items.english: Goods travelled only by means of the port of Seville.

items.spanish: Por medio del galeón, la plata americana llegaba a Asia.
items.english: By means of the galleon, American silver reached Asia.

items.spanish: A través de Manila llegaban a América la seda y la porcelana.
items.english: Silk and porcelain reached America through Manila.

items.spanish: Mediante el contrabando, otros países vendían sus productos a las colonias.
items.english: By means of contraband, other countries sold their goods to the colonies.

sections.content: After *mediante*, *por medio de* and *a través de* put a noun: never *mediante de*. They belong to a formal style, so they fit history texts better than everyday talk.
